transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net, my name is Ravi, how can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Ravi, I'm having trouble with my smart home devices, my light switches and my video doorbell keep going offline randomly, mostly in the evenings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sorry to hear that, let's get it sorted for you. Can I grab your account number, PIN, and the name on the account first?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, account is 512-330-871, PIN is 6620, and it's under Priya Nair.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, Priya, that all matches, you're verified. So just to confirm what I'm hearing: your smart switches and doorbell camera are dropping off your WiFi network intermittently, and it seems to happen more in the evenings specifically, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly right, yeah. During the day it's mostly fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, that evening pattern is a useful clue. How long has this been going on?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: About a week and a half now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, and did anything change around when it started, new devices added, router moved, anything like that?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually yeah, we added a couple more smart plugs last weekend, right before it got worse.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a really useful detail. How many smart devices total are on your WiFi now, roughly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me think... probably around fourteen now, between switches, plugs, the doorbell, and a couple of speakers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fourteen is a decent number. Are they all on the same WiFi network, or do you have a separate one for smart devices?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just the one main network, everything's on it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. And when it happens in the evening, is it all the devices at once, or does it seem more staggered?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: More staggered actually, like one device drops, then a few minutes later a different one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That staggered pattern combined with the evening timing and the added devices is pointing toward something specific. Does your household do a lot more WiFi usage in the evenings, streaming, gaming, video calls, that kind of thing?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah actually, that's pretty much exactly when everyone's home streaming shows and my husband games online.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That lines up well. A lot of routers have a limit on how many simultaneous device connections they handle smoothly, and streaming plus gaming traffic competing with fourteen smart devices for airtime can cause exactly this kind of staggered dropout, especially on an older or entry-level router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That actually makes a lot of sense, we never really thought about it that way.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How old is your current router, do you know?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's the one you guys gave us, so probably three or four years old at this point.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's a bit dated for handling this many devices plus heavy evening streaming and gaming. Let's check a couple of things before jumping to hardware though. Does the router have a 5 gigahertz band separate from the 2.4, and do you know which one the smart devices are on?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I think they're mostly on the 2.4 one, that's usually the default for smart home stuff isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, most smart plugs and switches only support 2.4 gigahertz, which is also the band your phones and laptops often default to as well, so it gets congested fast with that many devices sharing it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So too many things crammed onto one band basically.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. Let's check the router's connected devices list if you can pull that up, do you have the app or the web login handy?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, let me open the app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm in the connected devices screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, does it show a total count, and does it separate 2.4 versus 5 gigahertz connections?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shows nineteen total connected devices, and yeah there's a band column, looks like fifteen are on 2.4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Nineteen total with fifteen crowding the 2.4 band is genuinely a lot for an older router, that strongly supports the congestion theory, especially with the evening usage spike on top of it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wow, I had no idea it was that crowded.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It sneaks up gradually as you add devices over time. Let's try a couple of things. First, can you check if there's a QoS or Quality of Service setting in the app?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look... yeah, there's a QoS tab, it's currently off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's turn that on, it prioritizes traffic so streaming and gaming don't completely starve out your smart devices' connections.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, toggling it on now... done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good. Next, is your video doorbell on battery or wired power?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Battery.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Battery-powered doorbells sometimes go into a deeper power-saving sleep between events, which can look like a dropout even when it's not really a WiFi problem specifically. Does the doorbell app show a low battery warning at all?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check... no, it says seventy-eight percent, so that's probably not it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good to rule that out then, so this really does look like it's the network congestion. One more thing, does the router support creating a separate WiFi network just for smart devices, sometimes called an IoT network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm not sure, I've never looked for that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's check together, look under WiFi settings for something like 'Guest Network' or 'IoT Network'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found a Guest Network option, is that the same thing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It can work similarly, some routers let you rename it as a smart-home network specifically. Go ahead and enable it if you can, then we can start moving your smart devices onto that instead of your main network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, enabling it now... done, it's asking me to set a name and password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead and set those, then we'll walk through re-pairing a couple of your smart plugs onto it as a test.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, named it and set a password, ready when you are.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, pick one smart plug and open its app, then look for 'Change WiFi Network' or similar in its settings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it, changing to the new network now... okay, it says connected.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's exactly what we want to see. Over the next day or two, if you move the rest of your smart devices onto that dedicated network the same way, your main network will have a lot more room for streaming and gaming, and the smart devices won't be competing with them anymore.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's honestly a really clear explanation, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This whole thing has been kind of a headache though, especially since it started right after I added new devices I paid good money for.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, adding a bunch of new gadgets and expecting the same router to just handle it forever isn't really realistic, that's kind of just how home networks work as you scale up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I mean, sure, but it would've been nice to know that before I bought them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's not really something we'd proactively tell customers honestly, it's more on the individual to research that kind of thing beforehand.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, fair enough I guess.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Anyway, let's keep going, do you want me to walk you through moving the doorbell over to the new network too?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, that'd be great.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open the doorbell app, go to Device Settings, then WiFi, same idea as the plug.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay... it's asking to re-pair from scratch, is that normal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, doorbells often need a fresh pairing rather than a simple network switch, just follow the prompts, it usually takes about two minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, going through the pairing steps now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, it's showing connected and I can see live video again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's a good sign it picked up the new network cleanly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I move the light switches too, or leave those for now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'd recommend moving them over the next day or two as you have time, no rush, just prioritize whichever devices matter most to you first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Makes sense, I'll probably do the doorbell and a couple of key switches tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a good approach. While we're at it, do you want me to check if your account is eligible for a router upgrade, since this one is getting a bit old for your setup?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, that'd be helpful actually.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me pull that up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looks like you're eligible for a free upgrade to a newer mesh-capable router given your account tenure.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh nice, would that help with this specific issue too?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It would, a newer router handles a lot more simultaneous connections and has better band management built in, so it would reduce a lot of this congestion on its own even before the network split we just did.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds great, how would I go about getting that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can request the shipment for you right now if you'd like.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please, let's do that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Requesting it now... done, you should see it in five to seven business days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a fee for that upgrade at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, it's included with your current plan tier, no charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, one less thing to worry about.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the new router come pre-configured, or will I need to set everything up again from scratch?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You'll need to set your network name and password again, but I can send you a quick setup guide link after this call so it's straightforward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would be really helpful, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more thing, should I keep the smart-device network separate even after the new router arrives?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I'd keep that separation going forward regardless, it's just generally a healthier setup for a home with this many connected devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, I'll keep it that way then.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there anything else I should be doing in the meantime while I wait for the new router?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just keep moving devices over to the smart-home network as you get a chance, and leave QoS enabled, that combination should meaningfully cut down the evening dropouts even before the new router shows up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that's a solid plan, I appreciate you walking through all of this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This has actually restored some of my faith after that comment earlier about researching things myself.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fair enough, let's just focus on getting you sorted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sounds good. Is there a way to see historical connection drops, so I can tell if tonight's actually better?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under the app's Device History tab there should be a connectivity log you can check tomorrow morning to compare against tonight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect, I'll check that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do you think fourteen smart devices is actually a lot, or is that pretty normal these days?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's on the higher side for an older router but very normal for a newer mesh setup, so you're not doing anything unusual, the hardware just needed to catch up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, wasn't sure if we'd gone overboard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all, smart home setups like yours are getting more common all the time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's reassuring. Do the smart plugs need any special settings once they're on the new network, or is it plug and play?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Should be plug and play once you re-pair them, no special settings needed beyond picking the new network name.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, that simplifies things.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One last thing, is there a limit to how many devices that Guest or IoT network can support?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Typically similar limits to your main network, so you'll have plenty of headroom for your current fourteen devices and then some.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect, that answers everything I think.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually, one more, does the mesh router come with more than one unit, or just the one base station?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For your plan tier it ships with one base unit, but you can add satellite nodes separately later if you ever need wider coverage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know, our house isn't too big so probably won't need that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's usually the case for most single-story homes, one unit is typically plenty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the setup guide you mentioned cover the smart-home network split too, or just basic setup?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It covers both, there's a dedicated section for setting up a secondary IoT network on the new router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect, that'll be really helpful when it arrives.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I expect any downtime when I swap routers over?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just a few minutes while it reboots and devices reconnect, nothing major.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, I'll plan to do it on a weekend just in case.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a smart way to approach it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a way to track the shipment once it's sent?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, you'll get a tracking link by email once it ships, usually within a day or two.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, I'll keep an eye out for that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Last thing, does the doorbell need to be re-paired again once the new router arrives, or will it carry over?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You'll need to re-pair it once more to the new router's network, same quick process as today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, good to know ahead of time so it's not a surprise.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, I'd rather you know now than be caught off guard later.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I appreciate that, thanks again for all the help today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course, glad we got a good plan together.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks so much for the thorough help, Ravi.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net.
